title: IIT Delhi Researchers Successfully Transmit Quantum And Classical Data Over Single Fibre
key_facts: IIT Delhi researchers demonstrated the simultaneous transmission of quantum-entangled photons and classical data over a 50 km optical fibre link, according to a statement.
The research was led by Bhaskar Kanseri, a professor in IIT Delhi's Physics Department.
The practical problem: classical optical signals are much stronger than quantum signals and can generate noise that may disturb or obscure delicate quantum states.

Kanseri says quantum and classical communications can coexist over the same fibre 'under carefully controlled conditions', an important step toward joining quantum technology to existing telecom networks.
Sharing the same fibre could make such networks more scalable and cost-effective to deploy.
Funded by IIT Delhi's Institute of Eminence grant and the National Quantum Mission; published in the journal 'Optics Communication' (name as printed by Rediff).
Long-term uses named: enhanced security for communications of financial institutions, government agencies, healthcare organisations and critical infrastructure.
No outside comment, test conditions beyond 'carefully controlled', or deployment plan is given.
quote_evidence: IIT Delhi researchers have achieved a significant milestone in quantum communication, successfully demonstrating the simultaneous transmission of quantum-entangled photons and classical data over a 50-km optical fibre, paving the way for highly secure and scalable next-generation networks.
Our demonstration shows that quantum and classical communications can coexist over the same optical fibre infrastructure under carefully controlled conditions.

By making use of same fibre infrastructure for quantum and classical signal, networks could also become more scalable and cost-effective to deploy, said Bhaskar Kanseri, who led the research, in the statement.
why_it_matters_hint: Sharing existing fibre between quantum and ordinary signals could make quantum-secure networks cheaper and easier to roll out.
event_date: Statement reported 5 Oct 2026; the publication date of the paper is not stated.
